# Interview Experience – Amazon | SDE-2 (Senior Backend Engineer) 🧠💻 | Ravi Kumar · LinkedIn · 2026-01-21

**Ravi Kumar**: SDE-2 at Optym with 5 years of experience. Previous roles include SDE-2 at BlackBuck (Zinka Logistics Solutions Ltd), Senior Member Technical at Broadridge, and Coordiantor at Robotics Club MNNIT. Based in Bengaluru, Karnataka, India [IN].

---

Interview Experience – Amazon | SDE-2 (Senior Backend Engineer) 🧠💻
Recently completed the interview process at Amazon for an SDE-2 role.
It was intense, well-structured, and heavily focused on problem-solving, ownership, and depth.

Sharing a quick breakdown — hope this helps fellow backend engineers 🚀
🟢 Online Assessment (OA)
Coding Challenge (90 mins): 2 DSA problems, strong focus on edge cases, optimal solutions, and clean code
Work Simulation (15 mins): Real-world SDE decisions, prioritization, and trade-offs
Work Style Surveys (10 mins): Ownership, collaboration, and handling ambiguity
🟢 Coding Round
Q1: Longest Bitonic Subarray
(Expected both brute force + optimal approach with time/space analysis)
Q2: Modify a tree so all node values lie within a given range
(Traversal strategy, recursion, edge cases)
🟢 LLD Round
Designed a multi-turn chat system with LLM
Session management & conversation history
Context handling for multi-turn chats
APIs, caching, and cost optimization
Strong focus on design clarity and trade-offs
🟢 HLD Round
Designed a NoSQL database system
Discussed APIs, functional & non-functional requirements
Capacity constraints, data modeling, read/write patterns
🟢 Bar Raiser Round
Deep dive into my projects (HLD, decisions, impact, scalability)
Followed by a DSA question
Lots of “why?” — checking ownership and leadership mindset

No matter the outcome, it was a great learning experience.
On to the next one 🚀
If you’re preparing for backend/SDE-2 interviews, happy to help or discuss 🙂

# My Amazon SDE2 interview experience | Meghana Adiga · LinkedIn · 2026-05-05

**Meghana Adiga**: Based in Bengaluru, Karnataka, India [IN].

---

My [Amazon](https://linkedin.com/company/amazon) SDE2 interview experience
I recently went through the [Amazon](https://linkedin.com/company/amazon) SDE2 interview process. It was a good experience overall, although it did not result in an offer.

Round 1: Online Assessment
The assessment had three parts:
• Coding Challenge (90 mins): 2 questions similar to
https://lnkd.in/gft9UQBN
https://lnkd.in/gXqxdQ4z
• Work Simulation (15 mins)
Work through software development decisions faced by SDEs at [Amazon](https://linkedin.com/company/amazon)
• Work Style Surveys (10 mins)
Questions focused on how you approach engineering work and collaboration.

Round 2: Phone screening (60 mins) - This round decides whether you move forward to the onsite/loop interviews.
1 coding question similar to:
https://lnkd.in/gfYgDssx or
https://lnkd.in/g44VnwGM
followed by 2 follow-ups on the question

Loop Interviews:
Round 3: Coding – Data Structures & Algorithms  (60 mins)
https://lnkd.in/gjAJMgNT with 2 questions on Leadership Principles

Round 4: Coding – Problem Solving  (60 mins)
Coding question similar to https://lnkd.in/gYJGT8XU with 2 questions on Leadership Principles

Round 5: Coding – Logical & Maintainable (LLD)  (60 mins)
Design a Library Management System, followed by 2 Leadership Principle questions

Round 6: System Design (HLD + LLD)  (60 mins)
Design a Notification Service, followed by 2 Leadership Principle questions

Optional Candid Chat (30 mins)
I got this opportunity to speak with an Amazonian outside hiring team about culture, mentorship, and growth.

Leadership Principle Themes I Encountered
• Something cool I learned on my own
• A missed problem and how I fixed it
• Identifying and solving a customer pain point
• Handling challenging deadlines
• Choosing between multiple solutions
• Balancing quality vs speed
• Disagreeing with team decisions constructively

Key Takeaways
• Strong DSA fundamentals are essential, especially sliding window, greedy, and graph problems.
• Leadership Principles are deeply embedded in every round—prepare structured stories.
• System design and LLD clarity matter as much as coding at this level.
• Clear communication and reasoning, managing time matter more than just getting the correct answer.

Hope this helps anyone preparing for [Amazon](https://linkedin.com/company/amazon) SDE2.

# SDE II interview process at Amazon is a strong example of how deeply they evaluate your thinking and real-world experience. | Abhijeet Singh · LinkedIn · 2026-04-29

**Abhijeet Singh**: Software Engineer at HCLTech for 3 years 5 months with 3 years 10 months of total professional experience. Previous roles include Associate Engineer at HCLTech, Cloud Engineer at Wipro, and Machine Learning Intern at Allsoft Solutions and services Private Limited. Based in Greater Lucknow Area [IN].

---

SDE II interview process at Amazon is a strong example of how deeply they evaluate your thinking and real-world experience.

Recently, I went through the SDE II (Ads AI Core Infra) interview process at Amazon. Thought of sharing my experience here — it might help others preparing 👇

𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 𝟭 – 𝗗𝗦𝗔 / 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺 𝗦𝗼𝗹𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗴
Focused on problem-solving and approach clarity.
Graph/BFS based problem (similar to Bus Routes)
Discussion on optimization and edge cases
Emphasis on explaining thought process before coding
👉 Key takeaway: Don’t rush to code. Explain approach clearly.

𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 𝟮 – 𝗗𝗦𝗔 + 𝗙𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗼𝘄-𝘂𝗽𝘀
More depth on problem solving.
Greedy problem (similar to Jump Game)
Follow-ups on optimization and edge cases
Asked to explain code line-by-line
👉 Key takeaway: Be ready to defend your solution.

𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 𝟯 – 𝗟𝗟𝗗 / 𝗦𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺 𝗧𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴
Focused on design and real-world scenarios.
Design a system (like food delivery / listing services)
APIs, data flow, and caching discussion
Trade-offs and scalability considerations
👉 Key takeaway: Think in terms of systems, not just code.

𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 𝟰 – 𝗗𝗲𝗲𝗽 𝗗𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗼 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁𝘀
This was the most interesting round.
Detailed discussion on my work projects
Focus on performance optimization and backend logic
Questions around:
Why decisions were made
Trade-offs (memory vs performance)
Scalability and improvements
👉 Key takeaway: Know your project end-to-end. Be ready for deep follow-ups.

𝗢𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗹𝗹 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴
This process clearly shows that companies like Amazon evaluate:
Problem-solving ability
System thinking
Communication clarity
Real-world experience and ownership
It’s not just about writing correct code — it’s about how you think and explain.

𝗙𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗧𝗵𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵𝘁
Even though I didn’t make it through this time, the experience was a great learning curve.

# I recently went through the SDE-2 interview process at Amazon. | Shailendra Yadav · LinkedIn · 2026-04-19

**Shailendra Yadav**: Software development engineer 2 at Amazon for 6 months with 4 years 11 months of total professional experience. Previous roles include Senior Software Engineer at Texas Instruments and Full Stack Engineer at Societe Generale Global Solution Centre. Based in Bangalore Urban, Karnataka, India [IN].

---

I recently went through the SDE-2 interview process at Amazon.

And this one was proper intense — face-to-face 4 rounds + an eliminatory OA before that.

🎯 Round 0: Online Assessment (The Gatekeeper)
Before anything else, you have to clear this.

Coding + logical thinking + time pressure.
If you pass, you unlock the real game.

🎬 Round 1: DSA (Confidence vs Reality)
Problem looks simple. You feel good.

You solve it.
Interviewer: “Can you optimize it?”
You optimize.
Interviewer: “Any edge cases?”

At this point, even your confidence has edge cases.

🧩 Round 2: Low Level Design (Structure meets chaos)
Design a system with proper classes, APIs, flow.

You’re explaining clean design…
Then come the real questions:

“What if scale increases?”
“What about concurrency?”
“What breaks first?”

Now you're not designing. You're defending your design.

🏗️ Round 3: High Level Design (Think bigger)
Now it's architecture.

Services, databases, scaling, trade-offs.
You start talking in terms of systems instead of code.

And every decision needs a reason.

🧠 Round 4: Bar Raiser (Final Boss)
This round is different.

Ambiguous problems.
Deep follow-ups.
Lots of “why”.

They’re testing how you think, not just what you know.

🔥 Plot twist: Leadership Principles in EVERY round

This was the real game.

Every round had questions like:
“Tell me about a time you took ownership”
“Tell me about a failure”
“Tell me about a conflict”

And they go deep.

One answer = multiple follow-ups.

If your story is not real, it breaks quickly.

💡 What actually matters:

• Clear thinking > perfect answers
• Communication is everything (think out loud)
• Be ready to defend your decisions
• Have solid, real stories for Leadership Principles
• Depth > surface-level knowledge

🎯 Biggest takeaway:

It’s not about knowing everything.

It’s about how you think, communicate, and stay composed when you don’t.

If you're preparing for SDE-2 roles:

👉 Practice DSA and design
👉 But ALSO practice telling your experiences clearly (this is underrated)

Because at Amazon,
your stories matter as much as your solutions.

Happy to help if you're preparing — feel free to reach out.

#Amazon #SDE2 #InterviewExperience #LeadershipPrinciples #SystemDesign #DSA #CareerGrowth
